meta.title: Muscle fatigue: the EMG median-frequency shift
meta.tools: Physiological surface-EMG synthesis (motor-unit action potentials with slowing conduction velocity), median/mean frequency estimation
meta.summary: Show how slowing muscle-fibre conduction velocity during a sustained contraction compresses the EMG spectrum, predict the median-frequency decline from the velocity change, and measure the estimator's accuracy and variance on a synthetic 60-s contraction.
meta.problem: Why does the EMG spectrum shift to lower frequencies as a muscle tires, and how precisely can the shift be tracked?
meta.theory:
A motor-unit action potential travelling at conduction velocity v has a spectrum that scales with v: $S_v(f)=\frac{1}{v^2}\,S_1\!\left(\frac{f}{v}\right)$ (Lindström & Magnusson 1977).
Hence the median frequency is proportional to v: a 20 % fall in conduction velocity (typical over a fatiguing isometric contraction) lowers the median
frequency by 20 %. Spectral estimates from 1-s windows scatter by several percent.
meta.method:
Synthetic surface EMG (clearly labelled synthetic: no public dataset with ground-truth conduction velocity was available): 50 motor units, Poisson firing ~15 Hz,
tripolar MUAP shape whose time scale ∝ 1/v; v falls linearly from 4.5 to 3.6 m/s over 60 s; noise 20 dB below. Median frequency from Welch spectra in 1-s
windows (50 % overlap); linear regression of MDF(t).
meta.data: Synthetic (physiologically parameterised) — the ground-truth conduction velocity is known exactly.

rows.quantity: Relative median-frequency decline over 60 s (= relative velocity decline 20 %)

metrics.quantity: Scatter of 1-s MDF estimates about the trend
